prose.summary: Landscape architects plan and document outdoor spaces, coordinating design with grading, construction, planting and public requirements. Current postings combine design software with project management and construction administration. The role overlaps with architecture and urban planning, but its subject is the site and public realm rather than the building alone.
prose.day_to_day: The measured work moves between drawings, models, presentations and coordination. AutoCAD, Rhino, construction administration and project management are the strongest current signals, with urban design and sustainability also present. A designer may develop a site concept, test it against constraints and carry the work into documents used for approval and construction. Senior roles add project leadership and coordination with other disciplines.
prose.work_environment: The current openings are office or studio roles with a physical-site component. None of the 15 live openings is marked remote. Site review, public or client presentation and construction coordination make location a practical constraint even when drawing work can be done on a computer.
prose.getting_in: Most U.S. states require landscape architects to hold a state license, and the LARE is the standard examination route. The usual post-degree period is 2 to 5 years, depending on experience requirements, exam progress and the state board. In the readable posting requirements, bachelor's degrees are the most common level and the median stated experience is 3 years. Unlicensed landscape designer titles exist in the current listings, so supervised work can precede licensure.
prose.ladder: Early roles concentrate on production, modeling and parts of a site package. Later roles add project management, client decisions and construction administration. The measured routes also connect the field to urban planning, architecture, civil engineering and interior design, but licensed destinations add their own gates.
prose.suits: This career fits people who want design work shaped by real sites, public use and construction constraints. It requires patience with documentation and coordination, not only concept work. The absence of remote openings is a constraint for anyone who wants to work without regular access to projects and teams.
prose.misconceptions: Landscape architecture is not garden decoration. The postings ask for design software, construction administration, urban design and project management because the work has to be documented and built.
prose.who_qualifies: People with experience in site design, AutoCAD, Rhino, construction documents, urban design or project coordination hold several recurring signals. Urban planners have a 46 percent measured route toward the role in the adjacent-career data, while architects and civil engineers share parts of the technical context. The state license remains a separate gate where required.
prose.what_the_numbers_miss: Listings cannot show how much of a role is design, documentation, community process or field coordination. Two landscape architect titles can divide those responsibilities very differently.

steps.how: Check the landscape architecture board where you plan to practice. Most U.S. states require licensing, with the LARE serving as the standard examination route.
Show decisions across plan, grading or site constraints, presentation and construction documentation. Keep the evidence tied to the tools named in current postings.
Current listings include landscape designer as well as landscape architect titles. Use supervised work to build the experience required by the relevant jurisdiction.

prose.tools: AutoCAD and Rhino are the clearest current software signals, with Lumion, Revit and SketchUp also present. Tools matter because they carry the project from design into presentation and documentation. Construction administration and project management are equally important once responsibility moves beyond production.

faq.a: 2 to 5 years after the degree is the usual range. The timing depends on documented experience, exam progress and the state board.
